sections.h2: Who handles what in Santa Rosa County
sections.html:
The work is split three ways. The Property Appraiser (srcpa.gov) sets values and exemptions, the Tax Collector (srctc.com) mails and collects the bill, and a Value Adjustment Board hears appeals.

The chain runs like this. The appraiser fixes assessed value and exemption eligibility. The county commission, school board and other levying bodies set millage. The finished roll then goes to the collector, who prints and mails the notices. The bill goes to the last address on the roll. If your lender pays from escrow, the lender should ask for its own copy. Collector offices are in Milton, Midway, Pace and Jay.

  • Value, exemptions, name and address: Property Appraiser.
  • Bill, payment, delinquency, certificates: Tax Collector.
  • Appeals of assessments, denied exemptions and deferrals: Value Adjustment Board, made up of three county commissioners and two school board members or a special master.

Most seller questions can be settled with two calls. Ask the appraiser what the parcel is valued at and which exemptions it carries, then ask the collector what is owed and by when.

Notices normally go out by November 1 for the calendar tax year, and the gross figure is due March 31. Each month you wait trims the discount by a point.

Discounts and penalties on real estate taxes
Month paidDiscount or penalty
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone
April 1 onwardDelinquent, 3% penalty; advertising fees added May 1

If a discount window ends on a weekend or legal holiday, it stays open until the next business day. Getting the bill is the owner's job, so call the collector if none arrives.

A 3 percent penalty lands on April 1. After that date, only cashier's check, money order, cash or credit card is accepted. The amount you owe is fixed by the date the office actually receives your money.

Delinquent parcels are advertised for three weeks in a local paper, a job the county commission gives to the lowest bidder, and the cost is added to the delinquent bill. By June 1 the collector runs the certificate sale online through LienHub.com as a reverse auction. It opens at 18 percent interest and goes to the lowest bidder.

  • A certificate is a lien. Buying one gives the investor no ownership rights.
  • Costs jump at once when the county holds the certificate and someone buys it, or when a tax deed application is filed.
  • Years of nonpayment can end with the property being sold.

The investor has to wait two years from April 1 of the issue year before applying for a tax deed, and during the wait can't contact you to demand payment. Homestead parcels also carry an opening bid that includes half of the latest assessed value.

If you're selling in this position, ask for a fresh payoff statement. The total grows as costs are added.

The appraiser's posted dates give a homestead filing period of January 1, 2027 to March 1, 2027. The Persons 65 or Over and Deployed Service Member exemptions run January 1 to June 1, 2027.

You can file online. Search for your parcel on the appraiser's site and click Apply for Exemptions, after updating your Florida ID and vehicle registration to the home address. The ground rules: the home must be your permanent residence by January 1, and your filing must reach the appraiser by March 1. The first $25,000 counts against every levy. The additional amount reduces non-school levies only, on value above $50,000.

Florida lets a county or city add a senior exemption worth up to $50,000 by ordinance, within an income limit, plus a 25-year version for homes valued under $250,000. Ask the appraiser which Santa Rosa taxing authorities have enacted them. A $5,000 reduction is available to owners rated 10 percent or more for a service-connected disability.

A new buyer's parcel is reset to just value, and your exemptions leave when you do. The state reads change of ownership broadly. It covers a sale, a foreclosure and any transfer of legal or beneficial title, except where the same person stays entitled or the transfer goes to a spouse.

Watch for mail that offers a copy of your deed for a fee. The appraiser issues a Property Owner Protection Alert about these letters. The businesses sending them have no official role, and neither the Property Appraiser's office nor the Clerk of Courts took part. Skip the offer. If you need a copy of a recorded deed, ask the Clerk directly.

Deed stamps are $0.70 per $100 of price, and price includes any mortgage the buyer assumes. The Clerk collects at recording. A deed sale winner has to post a deposit equal to 5 percent of the bid, or $200 if that is larger.

Ask the closing agent to order a tax payoff and apply it at closing, so nothing is left on the parcel for the buyer. The collector's online parcel search shows the balance, and the Milton, Midway, Pace and Jay branches answer questions in person. With escrow, your loan servicer requests the bill, but you still want the payoff confirmed ahead of closing.

Know who answers what. Legal description, value, exemptions and name or address changes belong to the appraiser. Rates belong to the taxing authorities that hold advertised public hearings. Non-ad valorem charges typically cover fire departments, street lighting, paving and special local projects, so ask the agency named on the bill.

For a closer bill review, ask the appraiser how your assessed value compares with just value. That gap is the Save Our Homes benefit the buyer won't inherit. The state lists a 3.4% CPI for 2024 with a 3.0% cap, 2.9% for 2025 and 2.7% for 2026.

An unpaid tax bill is a problem to solve, not a barrier to selling. The balance is taken out of your proceeds at the closing table. A sensible order of steps:

  1. Call the collector for a current balance and, if anything is delinquent, a written payoff.
  2. Hand that number to the title company or closing agent.
  3. Check the appraiser's record for your exemption status and mailing address.
  4. Review the settlement statement to see the tax line and any proration before you sign.

A cash buyer can shorten the timeline because no lender is waiting on an appraisal, but the payoff and proration work the same way.

Think of the closing statement as your final tax audit. Match the tax line against the bill you printed, look for a proration credit that fits the date you hand over keys, and ask the closing agent to explain any figure that surprises you. Fixing a mistake before funding is far easier than chasing a refund afterward.

Bring a photo ID and your contract to any office visit, and write down the parcel number so staff can pull the right account quickly. Ask each office to confirm by email or letter whatever it tells you by phone, and keep those messages with your closing papers in case a question comes up later.

faqs.a: The gross amount is due by March 31, with bills mailed on or before November 1. Payments in November earn 4%, December 3%, January 2% and February 1%.
A 3 percent penalty is added on April 1 for unpaid real estate accounts. Advertising fees are added on May 1, and a tax certificate sale follows by June 1.
Use the Apply for Exemptions button on your parcel page at the appraiser's site. The posted homestead period for 2027 runs January 1 to March 1.
That falls to the Value Adjustment Board, which also takes denied exemptions and tax deferral appeals. A value petition is due within 25 days after the TRIM notice.

faqs.q: Does the county sell my house when I miss a payment?
faqs.a: Not at first. What gets sold is a tax certificate, a lien that starts at 18 percent interest. Only a later tax deed application can lead to the property itself being sold.
